upcoming_changes.description: Organize topics, and lightweight standalone “floater” cards, into configurable, drag-and-drop kanban-style boards and columns, all with a purpose built management UI and per-board access control
Enable pinned messages in chat channels.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Composer media optimization image convert enabled
upcoming_changes.description: Enables client-side conversion of JXL, HEIC, and animated GIF images before upload. JXL and HEIC are converted to JPEG, animated GIFs larger than the threshold are converted to animated WEBP.
Enables the redesigned admin dashboard that lets you pin custom reports and includes improved site traffic, engagement, and other analytics tied to community success and value.
Shows a floating category card when a category hashtag is clicked if the user has permission to view that category.
Enable the redesigned composer.
Let members choose which buttons appear in their composer toolbar, from their interface preferences.
Enable the discourse-workflows plugin.

Generates a concise /llms.txt when no custom file is uploaded. The document describes public discovery routes, the preferred Discourse MCP interface, and responsible agent access. To tune automated access, configure Slow down crawler user agents and Slow down crawler rate.
Enables a redesigned invite flow that lets admins invite someone directly as an admin. The invitee becomes a moderator on signup and an admin once the inviter confirms via email.
Allow members to sign up, accept invitations, and log in with one-time email codes (OTPs), without requiring a password.
Serve supported topics and topic lists as Markdown through .md URLs and requests with an Accept: text/markdown header. Normal visibility and profile privacy rules always apply.
Adds a “Me too” button to unsolved topics in support categories, letting members signal they’re experiencing the same issue and opt-in to notifications about the topic's solution.

Replace the separate New and Unread lists with a single unified New list that makes it easier for members to distinguish between new topics and topics with new replies. When enabled, the /new route shows a combined view with subtabs for Topics (new topics) and Replies (tracked topics with new replies), and the unread option is removed from the top menu.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Granular anonymous and logged in groups permissions
upcoming_changes.description: Makes group-based site setting permissions treat 'everyone' as 'all logged-in users', and enables the new 'anonymous_users' and 'logged_in_users' pseudogroups so admins can explicitly target anonymous visitors and authenticated users.
Enables improved crawler tracking which can better detect likely crawlers and ensure traffic reporting is more accurate.
This change introduces design modifcations to the Foundation theme in Discourse.
When adding tags while creating or editing a topic, show the tags the member has recently used on their own topics at the top of the list, before the most popular tags of the forum.
Replaces the special Uncategorized category with a standard category of the same name, and migrates all topics over to it.
This change renames the FAQ page to Guidelines. The FAQ page will still be available at /faq. The FAQ URL setting works as before.

Moves the navigation for user pages — profile, activity, notifications, messages, invites and preferences — out of the horizontal tab bars and into a dedicated sidebar panel, the way the admin area works. On mobile the panel is served from the hamburger menu.

Voice brings integrated voice and video rooms to Discourse, with screen sharing, background blur, noise suppression, live subtitles, direct calls, room chat, and group-based permissions. Members can keep browsing while they talk, with no external app required.

settings.humanized_name: Display local time in user card
settings.description: Display the local time based on a user's timezone when their user card is opened.
Support mixed left-to-right and right-to-left text directions
Allow usernames and group names to contain Unicode letters and numbers
Regular expression to allow only some Unicode characters within usernames. ASCII letters and numbers will always be allowed and don't need to be included in the allowlist
Allow users to choose their own language interface preference

Displays localized content for users based on their browser or user language preferences. Such content may include categories, tags, posts, and topics. Supported locales are set in Content localization supported locales.
List of supported locales that user content can be translated to. The site's default locale is always included. Requires Content localization enabled.

Show a language switcher in the header, allowing visitors to switch between translated versions of Discourse and user-contributed content. Uses languages defined in Content localization supported locales
Groups allowed to update localized content. Requires Content localization enabled.
Allow authors to update localizations of their own topics and posts via the post menu.
Serve localized content to web crawlers when Content localization enabled and Set locale from param is enabled. The list of supported locales is defined in Content localization supported locales.

settings.humanized_name: Content localization use default locale when unsupported
settings.description: Serve localized content in the site's default locale to users whose preferred language is not listed in 'content localization supported locales'.

settings.humanized_name: Set locale from accept language header
settings.description: Set interface language for anonymous users from their web browser's language headers
Allows setting an anonymous user's locale via the 'locale' browser cookie
Allows setting an anonymous user's locale via the 'tl' URL param, e.g. ?tl=es
The locale sent to onebox providers. If left blank, the default locale will be used
Timezone used to display dates in emails, must be a valid TZ
Enable the 'discourse-local-dates' plugin. This allows people to use '[date]' in posts to show readers dates in their local timezone

settings.humanized_name: Add rel nofollow to user content
settings.description: Add rel nofollow to all submitted user content, except for internal links (including parent domains). If you change this, you must rebake all posts with: "rake posts:rebake"
The likelihood that a flagged post will be hidden
Number of minutes a user must wait before they can edit a post hidden via community flagging
The likelihood that a new user will be silenced based on spam flags

settings.humanized_name: Num users to silence new user
settings.description: If a new user's posts exceed the Hide post sensitivity setting, and has spam flags from this many different users, hide all their posts and prevent future posting. 0 to disable.
If a user is automatically silenced, send a message to all moderators.
If a new user replies to a topic from the same IP address as the user who started the topic, flag both of their posts as potential spam.
How many times a new user can post a link to the same host within their `newuser_spam_host_threshold` posts before being considered spam.
A list of domains excluded from spam host testing. New users will never be restricted from creating posts with links to these domains.
When matching spammer emails, number of characters difference that will still allow a fuzzy match.

settings.humanized_name: Max new accounts per registration IP
settings.description: If there are already (n) trust level 0 accounts from this IP (and none is a staff member or at TL2 or higher), stop accepting new signups from that IP. Set to 0 to disable the limit.

settings.humanized_name: Min ban entries for roll up
settings.description: A new subnet ban entry will be created daily by the CleanUpUnmatchedIPs job when there are at least (N) blocked IP addresses within the same subnet.
Delete unmatched screened email entries after (N) days.
Delete unmatched screened IP entries after (N) days.
Minimum number of unique flaggers that is required to automatically pause a topic for intervention
The likelihood that a flagged topic will be automatically closed
Number of hours to pause a topic for intervention.
Enable automatic reply when disposing a flag.

Minimum amount of time a user must type for their first post. If the threshold is not met, the post will automatically enter the review queue. Low is 1 second, standard is 3 seconds, high is 5 seconds.

settings.humanized_name: Auto silence fast typers on first post
settings.description: Automatically silence users that do not meet Fast typing threshold

settings.humanized_name: Auto silence fast typers max trust level
settings.description: Maximum trust level to auto silence fast typers

Case insensitive regex that if passed will cause first post by user to be silenced and sent to approval queue. Example: raging|a[bc]a , will cause all posts containing raging or aba or aca to be silenced on first. Only applies to first post. DEPRECATED: Use Silence Watched Words instead.

settings.humanized_name: High trust flaggers auto hide posts
settings.description: New user posts are automatically hidden after being flagged as spam by a TL3+ user
How much time users will have to wait until they are able to reflag a post
Does 'Slow mode' prevent editing, after Editing grace period?
Does reviewable content need to be claimed before it can be acted upon?
Show reviewable content grouped by topic by default
Don't show reviewable items unless they meet this priority
The priority filter hides reviewable items that don't meet this score unless the '(any)' filter is used.
List of reasons that can be selected when rejecting a reviewable queued post with a revision. Other is always available as well, which allows for a custom reason to be entered.
How many minutes before a user can make a post with the same content again

upcoming_changes.description: Organize topics, and lightweight standalone “floater” cards, into configurable, drag-and-drop kanban-style boards and columns, all with a purpose built management UI and per-board access control
Enable pinned messages in chat channels.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Composer media optimization image convert enabled
upcoming_changes.description: Enables client-side conversion of JXL, HEIC, and animated GIF images before upload. JXL and HEIC are converted to JPEG, animated GIFs larger than the threshold are converted to animated WEBP.
Enables the redesigned admin dashboard that lets you pin custom reports and includes improved site traffic, engagement, and other analytics tied to community success and value.
Shows a floating category card when a category hashtag is clicked if the user has permission to view that category.
Enable the redesigned composer.
Let members choose which buttons appear in their composer toolbar, from their interface preferences.
Enable the discourse-workflows plugin.

Generates a concise /llms.txt when no custom file is uploaded. The document describes public discovery routes, the preferred Discourse MCP interface, and responsible agent access. To tune automated access, configure Slow down crawler user agents and Slow down crawler rate.
Enables a redesigned invite flow that lets admins invite someone directly as an admin. The invitee becomes a moderator on signup and an admin once the inviter confirms via email.
Allow members to sign up, accept invitations, and log in with one-time email codes (OTPs), without requiring a password.
Serve supported topics and topic lists as Markdown through .md URLs and requests with an Accept: text/markdown header. Normal visibility and profile privacy rules always apply.
Adds a “Me too” button to unsolved topics in support categories, letting members signal they’re experiencing the same issue and opt-in to notifications about the topic's solution.

Replace the separate New and Unread lists with a single unified New list that makes it easier for members to distinguish between new topics and topics with new replies. When enabled, the /new route shows a combined view with subtabs for Topics (new topics) and Replies (tracked topics with new replies), and the unread option is removed from the top menu.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Granular anonymous and logged in groups permissions
upcoming_changes.description: Makes group-based site setting permissions treat 'everyone' as 'all logged-in users', and enables the new 'anonymous_users' and 'logged_in_users' pseudogroups so admins can explicitly target anonymous visitors and authenticated users.
Enables improved crawler tracking which can better detect likely crawlers and ensure traffic reporting is more accurate.
This change introduces design modifcations to the Foundation theme in Discourse.
When adding tags while creating or editing a topic, show the tags the member has recently used on their own topics at the top of the list, before the most popular tags of the forum.
Replaces the special Uncategorized category with a standard category of the same name, and migrates all topics over to it.
This change renames the FAQ page to Guidelines. The FAQ page will still be available at /faq. The FAQ URL setting works as before.

Moves the navigation for user pages — profile, activity, notifications, messages, invites and preferences — out of the horizontal tab bars and into a dedicated sidebar panel, the way the admin area works. On mobile the panel is served from the hamburger menu.

Voice brings integrated voice and video rooms to Discourse, with screen sharing, background blur, noise suppression, live subtitles, direct calls, room chat, and group-based permissions. Members can keep browsing while they talk, with no external app required.

When matching spammer emails, number of characters difference that will still allow a fuzzy match.
